title: Interop strictness: strict on bytes and on what the drafts say; lenient on clear meaning; mimid's own policy choices are settings; franking and room policy are SHOULD
description:
Decided by Mark, 2026-11-14 (IETF 127 table), after a day of mimid vs Haven interop.

1. Wire format: strict. Trailing bytes, non-minimal lengths, unknown enum values and other malformed encodings are refused, sent and received. MLS signs and hashes exact bytes; several encodings of one value invite parser differentials.
2. Rules the drafts state: enforced, and a refusal cites the text. Examples: mls-extensions-11 §5 Safe AAD and app_components listing in leaves; room-policy-04 §8.1 role changes; protocol-07 §3.5 leave shape; §5.2 requiredCapabilities. When a peer trips one, show them the section; that is how today's Haven fixes happened.
3. Received meaning: lenient where it is unambiguous and harmless, on the requesting side only, with the divergence logged. Examples already in: KeyMaterialResponse::decode_for_requester (partialSuccess with no success read as noCompatibleMaterial, mimid-1wgh.46.1.7.1); reportAbuse 200 or 201 (mimid-1wgh.46.6.2). What mimid sends stays strict.
4. mimid's own policy choices beyond the drafts are deployment or room settings, not fixed rules.
5. Franking and room policy are SHOULD, not MUST, whatever the drafts say: a hosted room SHOULD require frank_aad and SHOULD carry a base_room_policy, but mimid's hub MUST NOT refuse a room, a member or a message because they are absent. Where they are absent the features that depend on them (franking-backed abuse reports; role-based authorization) are simply unavailable for that room, and mimid says so in its logs, not by refusing.

Supersedes, for hosting: mimid-1wgh.6.74 (hub requires frank_aad in safe_aad) and mimid-1wgh.6.57 (create_room requires a valid base_room_policy) — both become defaults, not requirements. Implementation: mimid-1wgh bead filed with this one. Related spec text to raise with the WG: franking and room policy as SHOULD (IETF notes/2026-11-14-mimi-issues-from-table-draft.md).
notes:
Follow-up decisions recorded on mimid-1wgh.53 (Mark, 2026-11-14): unfranked rooms accept abuse reports with messages marked unverified; require_franking and require_room_policy config keys, default false.
2026-11-14 (Mark): RFC 3986 §6.2.2 equivalence of user and room URIs is 'clear meaning': lookups use the normal form (commit 8761132). Not applied to signed values, MLS credentials or the participant list.
2026-11-18 (Mark via mimid-jf20; commit 22d5ec2, branch policy-defaults): narrowed. Open rooms (no base_room_policy) are now an explicit local choice: require_room_policy defaults to true and the hub hosts a policy-less room only if its operator sets it to false. Item 5's 'MUST NOT refuse a room because base_room_policy is absent' no longer holds for rooms this hub hosts; it still holds for members and messages of rooms already hosted, and for rooms other providers host (the follower relays them; their hub decides). Franking stays a SHOULD (require_franking default false).
